```{r}
#| label: setup-binary
#| include: false
# The numbers of the session on binary outcomes that the setup of the case does
# not hold, computed from the rows of the reference specification (ref_rows:
# the coded replies to Hispanic and white names) with the functions that
# companion/binary-outcomes.qmd uses. Comes after the two setup chunks and uses
# their data and formats.

# The two by two table of the reference comparison, with and without the
# continuity correction
chi_ref_yates <- unname(stats::chisq.test(tab_ref)$statistic)

# The linear probability model of the reference comparison, whose intercept is
# the share for the white names and whose coefficient is the difference, and
# the standard error of the difference computed group by group (the Welch
# t-test), beside the classical and the HC2 errors of the setup
lpm_coefs <- stats::coef(stats::lm(named ~ hispanic, data = ref_rows))
se_two_sample <- 100 * stats::t.test(named ~ hispanic, data = ref_rows)$stderr

# The predictions of a linear probability model with the covariates of the
# curve, which a straight line could carry outside 0 and 1
lpm_covariates <- stats::lm(named ~ hispanic + hard_email + pop_third + poverty_third + black_third + hispanic_third,
                            data = ref_rows)
lpm_range <- range(stats::fitted(lpm_covariates))

# The logit of the reference comparison on the model columns alone, because
# marginaleffects refuses a data column called group; its intercept is the log
# odds of a greeting for the white names
logit_cols <- datawizard::data_select(ref_rows, c("named", "hispanic", "hard_email"))
logit_fit <- stats::glm(named ~ hispanic, family = stats::binomial(), data = logit_cols)
logit_odds_white <- stats::coef(logit_fit)[["(Intercept)"]]
logit_b <- stats::coef(logit_fit)[["hispanic"]]
odds_ratio <- exp(logit_b)
ame_ref <- marginaleffects::avg_comparisons(logit_fit, variables = "hispanic")
preds_ref <- marginaleffects::avg_predictions(logit_fit, variables = list(hispanic = 0:1))

# The gap in points that the odds ratio of the data implies at four shares of
# greetings for the white names, and across the logits of the curve
or_bases <- tibble::tibble(white = c(0.20, 0.50, 0.611, 0.90)) |>
  datawizard::data_modify(gap = 100 * (stats::plogis(stats::qlogis(white) + logit_b) - white))
curve_logits <- datawizard::data_filter(curve, model == "logit")

# Non-collapsibility in numbers: two kinds of authority, equally many of each,
# whose white names are greeted by name 85% and 35% of the time, and a
# Hispanic name that multiplies the odds of a greeting by the odds ratio of the
# data in both kinds; the odds ratio for all authorities together
two_kinds <- tibble::tibble(white = c(0.85, 0.35)) |>
  datawizard::data_modify(hispanic = stats::plogis(stats::qlogis(white) + logit_b),
                          gap = 100 * (hispanic - white))
all_white <- mean(two_kinds$white)
all_hispanic <- mean(two_kinds$hispanic)
odds_ratio_all <- exp(stats::qlogis(all_hispanic) - stats::qlogis(all_white))

# How well the hard-to-find address predicts the greeting, and how evenly
# chance spread the Hispanic names across the two kinds of address
white_named <- ref_rows |>
  datawizard::data_filter(group == "white") |>
  datawizard::data_summary(named_share = 100 * mean(named), by = "hard_email")
block_shares <- ref_rows |>
  datawizard::data_summary(hispanic_share = 100 * mean(hispanic), by = "hard_email")
```
